disposition_mapping.rationale: Issue of the calendar and central planning assumptions, including the downside macro scenario input required by ABB-R-01 and ABB-R-10, is carried forward substantially unchanged, now published through a shared workbench for consistency across submitters.
Top-down target setting is unconstrained by design and is retained with no structural change, aside from explicit visibility of downside-scenario target ranges.
Revenue and volume planning (ABB-R-02) is preserved but restructured into a driver-based workbench that improves traceability of assumptions without changing ownership by business unit heads.
Cost centre and headcount budgeting (ABB-R-03) is preserved but restructured onto the same driver-based platform as revenue planning for consistency and auditability, ownership unchanged.

Capex request submission is restructured to enforce, via system control, that any request above threshold cannot proceed without the business case input required by ABB-R-04; the function and its evidentiary requirement persist.

Consolidation into a draft three-statement budget (ABB-R-06) is restructured into an automated engine but continues to consume accounting policies applied to actuals (ABB-R-05/KB-06) and central FX assumptions (ABB-R-07/KB-07), adding explicit intercompany-elimination visibility per KB-14 and an exceptions log supporting faithful representation (KB-02).
Review and challenge iterations are unconstrained by design and retained, enhanced only with scenario/sensitivity views to make the downside case more actionable in challenge sessions.
Board approval (ABB-R-11) is retained unchanged and continues to precede load-and-lock, preserving the ordering required by ABB-R-08.

Loading and locking of the approved version (ABB-R-09) is retained, occurring strictly after board approval (ABB-R-08), with an added audit trail of the prior draft and exceptions for evidential support (KB-02, KB-03).

steps.description: The FP&A manager issues the budget calendar and central planning assumptions (inflation, FX, interest rates) together with at least one downside macro scenario, published through a shared planning workbench so all submitters work from a single assumption set.
steps.name: Issue calendar, central planning assumptions and scenarios

steps.description: CEO/CFO set top-down revenue, margin and cost targets against the strategic plan and the published central planning assumptions, including a target range under the downside scenario.
steps.name: Set top-down targets

steps.description: Business unit heads prepare and own revenue and volume plans in a driver-based planning workbench, with assumptions traceable to the central planning assumptions and visible scenario sensitivity to the downside case.
steps.name: Driver-based revenue and volume planning

steps.description: Cost centre owners prepare and own cost centre and headcount budgets in the same driver-based workbench, with headcount and cost drivers linked to the central planning assumptions for consistency and audit traceability.
steps.name: Driver-based cost centre and headcount budgeting

steps.description: Business unit heads submit capex requests through the workbench; any request above the materiality threshold is blocked from submission until a documented business case is attached, enforcing the evidentiary basis for capitalisation decisions.
inputs: Business case for capex above threshold
steps.name: Capex requests with mandatory business case above threshold

steps.description: An automated consolidation engine aggregates revenue, cost, headcount and capex submissions into a draft P&L, balance sheet and cash flow on the same accounting basis and using the same accounting policies as actuals, applying central FX assumptions for translation and flagging intercompany positions for elimination; the three statements are system-reconciled and exceptions are routed to the FP&A analyst for resolution.
steps.name: Automated consolidation and reconciliation into draft three-statement budget

steps.description: The draft budget is reviewed and challenged in iterations with submitters, using scenario and sensitivity views (including the downside scenario) to pressure-test assumptions before escalation to the board.
steps.name: Review and challenge iterations

steps.description: The board reviews and approves the revised budget, including the downside scenario implications, before any version is loaded into downstream systems.
steps.name: Board approval

steps.description: The board-approved budget is loaded into the planning system and locked as the single version of record used by variance analysis and rolling forecasts, with the prior draft and exception log retained for audit trail.
steps.name: Load and lock approved version

steps.description: The locked budget version is connected to the rolling forecast process so that subsequent actuals and reforecasts are compared on a consistent policy and FX basis, closing the loop between the annual budget build and in-year forecasting without altering the locked version itself.
steps.name: Establish rolling forecast linkage
